gaps.explanation: Statement lines are the accrual Statement of Revenues, Expenditures, and Changes in Net Position - Proprietary Funds, Totals 2022 (pp9-10, printed pp14-15): Charges for services 1,940,964 + Lease agreement 90,147 + Insurance proceeds 7,407 + Miscellaneous 8,449 = Total operating revenues 2,046,967, + Interest revenue 9,446 = 2,056,413. The only business-type schedule is Schedule 29 'Statement of Cash Receipts and Cash Disbursements Compared to Budget' (p35, printed p69), Actual Budgetary Basis receipts per fund: Electric 1,607,843 + Water 324,090 + Sewer 254,034 = 2,185,967 (detail lines for Electric/Water/Sewer, read correctly). Per fund the budgetary receipts differ from the accrual revenues (Electric 1,607,843 vs 1,463,539 + 8,908 = 1,472,447; Water 324,090 vs 332,216 + 391 = 332,607; Sewer 254,034 vs 251,212 + 147 = 251,359); the budgetary basis counts cash receipts (incl. capital/interfund cash items such as disposition of capital assets 15,691 and restricted-asset/deposit movements on the p11 cash flow statement) rather than accrual revenue. Schedule above the statement by 129,554 because of the basis; no line missing or doubled.

Statement (pp9-10, accrual Totals 2022): Production and purchased power 993,402 + Maintenance and operation 399,531 + General 57,360 + Administrative 113,443 + Depreciation 236,782 + Loss on disposition of assets 39,883 + Interest expense 9,344 = 1,849,745. Schedule 29 (p35) Actual Budgetary Basis disbursements: Electric 1,310,090 + Water 158,453 + Sewer 198,790 = 1,667,333 (detail, one printed line per fund). The statement includes non-cash depreciation 236,782 and loss 39,883 (276,665) that the budgetary schedule excludes, and the schedule includes cash items the statement capitalizes or carries on the balance sheet (p11: purchase of capital assets 135,404, principal paid 23,979, consumer deposits 63,652). Per fund: Electric 1,310,090 vs 1,283,916 + 39,883 = 1,323,799; Water 158,453 vs 282,682; Sewer 198,790 vs 233,920 + 9,344 = 243,264. Printed totals 1,849,745 and 1,667,333 genuinely differ by basis (schedule short by 182,412); the one-line-per-fund schedule cannot be reconciled further.
